newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to decide on liquor taxes by end-Dec - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to decide on liquor taxes by end-Dec - MOF.

text.p: Japan will decide by the end of this month on how it will conform its rules to comply with the World Trade Organisation's ruling that its tax system treats foreign spirits unfairly, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Wednesday.
"We are currently debating how to comply with the ruling in the government tax panel and the Liberal Democratic Party's tax study group. We have not yet reached a decision," he said.
However, he added that Japan will decide by the end of December on what steps can be taken to revise the tax system in the next fiscal year in order to abide by the WTO ruling.
Japan usually comes up with the annual revision of its tax system in December, to be implemented from the following fiscal year starting in April.

Japanese newspapers reported earlier that the ministry is negotiating with the ruling Liberal Democratic Party to raise taxes on shochu, a popular domestic liquor made from materials such as barley, to around 12 yen per degree of alcohol, which would be about two to three times its current rate.
At the same time, it plans to lower the tax on whiskey to about half of its current rate of 24.56 yen per degree of alcohol, the papers said.

The reports also said that although the ministry wants to start implementing the measures gradually over a span of three to five years, European countries want the measures to be introduced all at once from the fiscal year starting on April 1, 1997.

MOF officials have said there are three options available if Japan chooses to comply with the WTO ruling -- raise taxes on shochu, lower taxes on foreign spirits such as whiskey or a combination of both.

The senior MOF official declined to comment on which option the government was most likely to take, but said that only lowering taxes on foreign spirits was "quite difficult" taking into account Japan's tight fiscal finances.
